task.description: The hard ceiling is 250 and AGENTS.md says split at about 200, so this is the backlog between the two. Counted with wc -l today: miter 31, storypole 8, benchwork 5, outfeed 4, chalkline 3, joiner 2, common 2, sawhorse 1, rabbet 1, dado and batten 0. Worst offenders: benchwork xray_service 249, miter security/mod 248, benchwork spec_studio 247, storypole core_cmds 246, miter polyglot language 246 and markdown 245. OF-32 already cleared the six outfeed-core modules that used to sit here, so this is the same sweep applied to the rest. Suggested order: miter polyglot modules together (they share context), then benchwork services, then storypole cli handlers. Run miter slice per file for the blueprint.

events.description:
RE-MEASURED 2026-10-31 after MTR-20 split miter-engine into four crates. The class has grown from the 60 files this was filed against to 85 files in the 200-250 band (miter audit --threshold 200, all under the hard 250 ceiling, so nothing is illegal yet).

Distribution: miter 37, benchwork/web 9, storypole 8, common 8, sawhorse 5, benchwork 5, outfeed 4, joiner 4, plus a tail.

The filing assumption that 31 of the 60 were in miter-engine no longer holds - those files are now spread across miter-polyglot, miter-analysis, miter-inventory and miter-engine, and the count in miter as a whole went up rather than down, because the split moved files without shrinking them. That is the argument for doing this sweep now rather than after more extraction: the band is where the next 250-line breach will come from, and every extraction so far has pushed a file into it.
